input: Write a due diligence memo on Deel

output.company: Deel, Inc. (global HR, payroll and Employer-of-Record platform, founded 2019, Y Combinator)

business.claim: Deel sells a global HR platform for hiring, paying and managing workers across countries. It covers onboarding (contracts, equipment), global payroll, HR management for any worker type, and compliance with local labor laws.
Customers range from startups to enterprises. Named logos include Shopify, Nike, Klarna, Intuit, Uber, Coinbase and Anthropic (company claim).
Described as a New York-headquartered, fully remote company that processes about $22B in payroll a year. It plans to extend native payroll coverage to 100+ countries by 2029.
Expanding into identity verification and security tools by acquiring Tel Aviv AI-security/deepfake-detection startup Clarity (reported at about $40-50M).

Aggregator (StockAnalysis) lists Clarity as Deel's 15th acquisition, valued at up to $50M in cash and shares, plus the earlier PayGroup acquisition (AU$121M, completed Nov 2022). It also lists 2026 product moves: Deel Retirement (US 401(k) with Human Interest and Basic Capital), stablecoin payouts (MoonPay, Mesh, Stripe wallet) and a Workday Global Payroll Connect integration.

traction.claim: More than 40,000 customers (company claim, as of first half of 2026).
40,000+ supported businesses, 650,000+ workers hired and 175 customer case studies (company claim; the same page also shows 35,000+ customers, so it is internally inconsistent).
Customer count grew from 4,500+ at the Series D to 40,000+ by 2026 (company claims).
traction.date: page last updated 2026-06-03; original announcement date not shown

traction.claim: Partnerships listed by aggregator StockAnalysis (dates approximate from relative timestamps): Microsoft Marketplace listing (2026-07-27), MoonPay stablecoin payouts (2026-02-10), Stripe stablecoin wallet (~Mar 2026), Arsenal FC sleeve sponsorship from the 2026/27 season (~May 2026), DualEntry ERP (~Oct 2026).

team.claim: Alex Bouaziz is CEO and co-founder; he previously co-founded Sarona Ventures.
Shuo Wang is CRO and co-founder; previously co-founder and CTO of Aeris Cleantec, which iRobot acquired.
Joe Kauffman was appointed President and CFO. He spent more than 10 years at Credit Karma as CFO, President and CEO.
Philippe Bouaziz, founding CFO since 2019 and father of CEO Alex Bouaziz, moved to the newly created role of executive chairman and chief strategy officer.
Aggregator (StockAnalysis) lists Ofer Simon as a third co-founder. Deel's own about page does not confirm this.
Other named staff: Andrea David Mieli (head of legal) and Asif Malik (associate legal director), both named in the Irish High Court proceedings.

funding.claim: Series E: $300M at a $17.3B valuation, led by new investor Ribbit Capital, with Andreessen Horowitz, Coatue, General Catalyst and Green Bay Ventures. Total raised is nearly $1.3B since 2019.
The Series E valuation was a step up from a $12B prior valuation, per aggregator StockAnalysis.
Series D: $425M at a $5.5B valuation, led by Coatue, with Altimeter, a16z, Neo, Spark Capital, YC Continuity, Green Bay Ventures and angels.
funding.date: page last updated 2026-06-03; original announcement date not shown

funding.claim: Last known valuation is $17.3B (Oct 2025 Series E). No new primary round was found in 2026.

Secondary market (aggregator StockAnalysis): $29.24 per share as of 2026-11-09, at the bottom of its 52-week range ($29.24-$34.53). That is down 14.33% year-to-date and 9.61% over one year. IPO is expected but no date is set.

financial_signals.claim: ARR passed $1.5B in the first half of 2026, after passing $1B in 2025 (company claim reported by Calcalist).
First $100M revenue month in September 2025. Deel says it has been profitable for three consecutive years (company claim).
Press page says revenue is above $1.5bn (company claim, undated).
About $800M annual run rate as of Feb 2025, per CNBC as cited by aggregator StockAnalysis. That implies roughly 1.9x growth to $1.5B ARR by H1 2026, calculated from company figures.
Headcount: 4,000+ team members in 100+ countries (company claim); aggregator StockAnalysis lists 5,000 employees. No layoffs found.

legal_and_regulatory.claim: Rippling (People Center, Inc.) sued Deel in the Northern District of California in March 2025 under federal RICO and trade-secret law. It alleges Deel paid Rippling employee Keith O'Brien to take trade secrets, citing 6,000+ Slack searches and 600+ customer records accessed. Deel confirms a payment of about $6,000 but disputes what it was for.

On 2026-09-25 Judge Charles Breyer denied Deel's bid to bar O'Brien's testimony, saying Deel 'actively avoided efforts' to resolve the dispute. He reaffirmed his February 2026 ruling that keeps Rippling's RICO and trade-secret claims alive. He sent Deel's racketeering claims against Rippling to arbitration, partly narrowed Deel's 32 Lanham Act counts, and dismissed its cybersquatting and trademark claims. No trial date was reported.

The DOJ (US Attorney, N.D. Cal.) reportedly issued grand jury subpoenas about the alleged spy plot, per the WSJ. Deel said it was 'not aware of a criminal investigation' and would cooperate. No charges were found.

Rippling's June 2025 amended complaint alleges CEO Alex Bouaziz was the 'chief architect' of the scheme. In November 2025 Rippling said unsealed documents show Deel paid the alleged spy and booked it as an expense (allegations, unproven).

Deel sued Rippling in Delaware in April 2025, alleging abuse of lawsuits, regulatory complaints and misleading marketing. Deel also says a Rippling intelligence manager accessed its platform 58 times under a fake company name.

Irish High Court (Justice Mark Sanfey): the joinder of CEO Bouaziz, Andrea David Mieli and Asif Malik as defendants was set aside. Rippling's case continues against Deel Inc, which accepted jurisdiction. Rippling discontinued its claim against O'Brien in August 2025 under a cooperation agreement.

Damian v. Deel, a suit by the receiver for Surge Capital Ventures alleging Deel helped Russian entities evade US sanctions by processing Surge payments, was dismissed by a Florida court. The article does not say whether the dismissal was with or without prejudice.

reputation.claim: Trustpilot (aggregator, user reviews): TrustScore 4.5/5 from 9,760 reviews, 1,663 of them in the last 12 months. 90% are 5-star and 5% are 1-star.

Recurring complaints on Trustpilot: late payouts and slow withdrawals (including funds stuck after a partner bank's license was revoked), KYC/identity verification failures and locked accounts, generic support replies, unpaid expense reimbursements, unexpected offboarding fees, and a report of a hacked account with stolen funds.
Sustained critical press over the Rippling espionage dispute, including reports of a DOJ criminal probe that analysts say could complicate IPO plans.

red_flags.claim: Reported DOJ criminal investigation (grand jury subpoenas) into the alleged spying on Rippling.
Rippling's civil RICO and trade-secret claims survived dismissal and reconsideration. Deel lost its bid to exclude the key witness, and its own racketeering claims were sent to arbitration.
The allegations name the CEO personally as the architect of the scheme. Deel admits the roughly $6,000 payment to the alleged spy but disputes its purpose.
Parallel espionage litigation continues against Deel Inc in the Irish High Court.
Governance: the CFO from founding until Nov 2025 was the CEO's father, who is now executive chairman.
Secondary-market price is down 14% year-to-date and at its 52-week low (aggregator data).
Customer complaints about payout delays and funds stuck after a partner bank's license was revoked suggest payments and partner-bank operational risk.
Company-published metrics are inconsistent: customers shown as 35,000+ and 40,000+, funding as $600M+ and $650M, against nearly $1.3B per Crunchbase.

output.verdict: Deel's scale is strong: it reports more than $1.5B in ARR (H1 2026, up from about $800M in Feb 2025), over 40,000 customers in 150 countries, claimed profitability, a $17.3B Series E led by Ribbit in Oct 2025, and a public-company CFO hired ahead of an IPO. The Rippling espionage matter needs a much closer look. The RICO and trade-secret claims have survived, there is a reported DOJ grand jury probe, the allegations implicate the CEO, and a parallel Irish case is running, all of which put leadership and the IPO at risk. Diligence should also cover the father-son governance history, the soft secondary pricing, and payout and partner-bank complaints from customers.
